newsitem.title: UK: Increased caper demand, rates up on freight market.
newsitem.headline: Increased caper demand, rates up on freight market.

text.p: Brokers reported more demand for capers in the Atlantic and stronger rates for large modern craned tonnage from the Continent to the Far East. But conditions for Panamaxes were again generally weaker and the BFI fell 7 points to 1,420.

Grain - The disruption of barge traffic affecting grain exports from the Mississippi and the falling freight market in the Far East have seen Panamaxes heading for Argentina and Brazil from the Continent and Mediterranean as well as the North Pacific. Not surprisingly South American rates were under heavy pressure. Toepfer followed its economical fixture of last Friday of Chryssoula l for 50,000/5 heavy grain 2 ports E Coast S America/Continent for end-April at $17.25 basis 2-1 with 55,000 heavy on an unnamed vessel Santos/Continent for 26 April/6 May at a depressed $15.00. The only Panamax reported fixed from Us Gulf was the Forest Ships-relet Halla Fortune for 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for 28 April/12 May at $23.75 no combo, down 25 cents from Continental's fixture just over a week ago of Royal Ocean for 15/25 April. Minerals etc - brokers said about 8-10 new enquiries were quoted for capers in the Atlantic and that the Pacific appeared steadier for these vessels. Krupp fixed Fortune 22 for about 160,000 iron ore Saldanha/Taranto for end May but reported rates of $6.35 and terms of 7 shinc were said to be inaccurate. Kleimar's fixture of Anne (Ex Pawnee) for 100,000/10 iron ore Nouadhibou/Antwerp at $4.17-1/2 and BHP's fixture of World Nord 151,000 dwt delivery Japan end April for a trip via east Australia to Rotterdam at $14,000 daily were said to have both failed. Panamax rates in the east continued to decline with even early modern tonnage struggling to obtain mid-$11,000's daily for Pacific or Australian rounds. Merchant Pioneer 69,763 dwt was said to be working Seatrans for coal Roberts Bank/Alexandria at about $17.00 and Cobelfret booked Great Nancy for 6000 tonnes Roberts Bank/Fos at $12.60. North Emperor 68,308 dwt was finally covered delivery prompt Japan for a cargo of sulphur from USWC to India by E.A.S.T.

handy-sizes - Large modern craned bulkers were said to be in strong demand from the Continent. You Yi 43,000 dwt, for example, was believed fixed for about $13,900 daily by Albatross for a trip to Singapore-Japan range. The Pacific was an erratic market for all but the most modern geared tonnage - Pisces Pioneer 35,310 dwt was booked by Hugo Neu for scrap from Los Angeles to S Korea at a lump sum of only $650,000. The 1983-built World Umpire 47,263 dwt obtained only a relatively weak level of between $8,500 and $8,750 daily from HMM delivery China for a Brazilian round voyage.
